source.product: No real product. An invented generic low three-seat Japandi sofa created for the hackathon demo catalogue; it does not depict or reproduce any manufacturer's design, and its price is invented demo data.
source.generation: Four-view turnaround reference sheet generated with the codex-image skill (front, three-quarter-front-left, side profile, rear on a seamless white studio backdrop under soft even diffused light, with only a contact shadow under the feet), cut into four images with scripts/turnaround_crop.mjs, then Higgsfield generate_3d model multi_image_to_3d with all four views as role "image": should_texture=true, enable_pbr=true, should_remesh=true, topology=triangle, target_polycount=28000, symmetry_mode=auto, rigging and animation false, plus a texture_prompt describing very pale oatmeal cream washed slub linen and short slim dark-stained oak feet.
source.postProcessing: Identical mesh to cream-linen-sofa. Only the glTF JSON chunk differs: pbrMetallicRoughness.baseColorFactor set to [0.3839, 0.1737, 0.0748, 1.0] (linear), computed from the delivered fabric mean #d6d2cc toward #8b5e3c. BIN chunk and textures copied byte for byte, so geometry, pivot and dimensions are identical by construction.

material.baseColorFactorNote: The single material declares no baseColorFactor, so the glTF default [1, 1, 1, 1] applies. A brown variant can be derived by adding baseColorFactor without removing or replacing anything.
material.metallicRoughnessNote: metallic ~0, roughness ~0.58 from the metallicRoughness texture; matte and non-metal, so a tint reads as fabric rather than plastic.

knownLimitations: Dimensions are a visual proxy, not a measured product, but the fit is exact: 210.0 x 90.0 x 75.0 cm against the intended 210 x 90 x 75, residual 0.00 cm on all three axes, footprint centred at x=0 z=0 and minY = 0.0 cm. fit_glb.py exited 0 at 9.40% anisotropy, just inside its 10% cap, so the asset passes the 2 cm / 3% tolerance in backend/api/test_furniture_assets.py without a budget entry.

The whole sofa is a single mesh with a single material, so the fabric and the feet share one baseColorTexture. Tinting the material with baseColorFactor to derive the brown variant will also darken the feet, which are already a dark warm brown at about #402817; they will go nearly black rather than staying oak.

The material carries emissiveFactor [1, 1, 1] with an emissiveTexture, which would normally add an untintable glow on top of any baseColorFactor. The emissive texture is solid black in this asset (maximum luminance 0 over all 1024x1024 texels), so it contributes nothing and will not dilute a brown tint. It must not be replaced with a non-black image.

The fabric measures a light neutral #d6d2cc rather than the palette's warmer #e9e4d8 cream: about 8% darker in luminance and noticeably less yellow. A brown multiplier will therefore read slightly cooler and more desaturated than the same multiplier over a warm cream, and may want a warmer or more saturated brown factor to compensate.

Seat height was not measured directly. The vertex distribution is dense between 35 and 45 cm, which is consistent with the intended ~42 cm seat, but this is inferred from geometry statistics rather than measured.
Reconstructed from generated reference images, not from photographs of a real object; small-scale detail such as seam placement, piping and the exact cushion split is approximate.

No render and no manual Blender inspection has been done. Verification is numeric only: bounding box, footprint centring, floor contact, triangle count, per-slab vertex distribution (feet correctly inset at X +/-95 cm and Z -40..38 cm under a body at X +/-105 cm and Z +/-45 cm, with no stray fragments), and texture colour statistics. The underside of the seat was not inspected and may be a flat untextured cap as on other assets in this batch.
Fabric and feet share one material, so the brown factor also darkens the already-dark oak feet. Cosmetic, and preferable to tinting the fabric muddy.
